chunks: I and Kāmil al-Tammār entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام). Kāmil said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, there is a hadith narrated by so-and-so.” He said, “Mention it.” He said, “It was narrated to me that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) spoke to ʿAlī (عليه السلام) of a thousand gates on the day the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) passed away; each gate opens a thousand gates, so that is a thousand thousand gates.”

He said, “That indeed was so.” I said, “May I be sacrificed for you, has that become manifest to your Shiʿah and your loyal followers?” He said, “O Kāmil, one gate or two gates.” So I said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, then from a thousand thousand gates of your merit, only one gate or two gates are narrated?”
He said: Then he said, “And what could you possibly narrate of our merit? What you narrate of our merit is nothing but a thousand not joined together.”

key_terms.أَلْفُ أَلْفِ بَابٍ: a thousand thousand gates, i.e. an immense multitude of branches of knowledge
key_terms.بِأَلْفِ بَابٍ: with a thousand gates, meaning major divisions or openings of knowledge
key_terms.شِيعَتِكُمْ: your Shiʿah, the followers devoted to the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.غَيْرَ مَعْطُوفَةٍ: not joined together, meaning disconnected or not comprehensively linked
key_terms.فَضْلِكُمْ: your merit or excellence, referring to the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.يَفْتَحُ أَلْفَ بَابٍ: opens a thousand gates, indicating expansive branching knowledge

ai.seo_question: How much of the knowledge and merits of the Ahl al-Bayt have been transmitted to people?
ai.summary: This hadith speaks of the vast body of knowledge imparted by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام at the end of the Prophet’s life. It emphasizes that only a very small portion of the merits and knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام has reached the Shiʿah. The narration highlights the immensity of their divinely granted knowledge and virtue.
